scenes.vo: For thirty days, a stranger paid for my chai. On day thirty, I followed him.
scenes.cap: 30 days, a stranger paid for my chai. Day 30, I followed him.

scenes.vo: Every morning, same stall. I'd reach for my wallet, and the chaiwala would say, already paid. By the man in the blue cap.
scenes.cap: "Already paid." By the man in the blue cap.

scenes.vo: I thought he wanted something. A favour. A loan. So I finally caught up with him at the bus stop.
scenes.cap: What did he want? I caught him at the bus stop.

scenes.vo: He laughed. Twenty years ago, on the worst morning of his life, a stranger bought him tea before a job interview.
scenes.cap: 20 years ago, a stranger bought HIM tea before a job interview

scenes.vo: He got the job. He never found that stranger. So every month, he picks someone, and pays for their chai.
scenes.cap: He got the job. Never found the stranger. So every month he picks someone.

scenes.vo: I asked how to pay him back. He said, don't. Just pick someone tomorrow.
scenes.cap: "How do I pay you back?" "Don't. Pick someone tomorrow."

scenes.vo: So tomorrow, somewhere, a stranger's chai is on me. Maybe it's yours.
scenes.cap: Tomorrow, a stranger's chai is on me. Maybe yours.
